title: FSSAI and Trademark Planning for Packaged Spice Businesses in Kattappana
metaTitle: FSSAI & Trademark Guide for Kattappana Spices | BRNDNUR
metaDescription: Essential dual compliance guide for Kattappana spice packagers and traders. FoSCoS licensing, spice packaging rules, and Trademark Classes 30 & 35.
intendedAudience: Spice auction merchants, cardamom grading plant owners, pepper packagers, and value-added agro-processors in Kattappana and Vandanmedu.
quickAnswer: Packaged spice enterprises in Kattappana must secure statutory FSSAI licensing via the FoSCoS portal (Basic Registration or State License depending on annual turnover) while concurrently filing trademark applications under Class 30 (for whole and ground spices) and Class 35 (for wholesale and retail distribution). Operating without trademark registration leaves your commercial packaging exposed to counterfeiters.

h2Sections.h2: Kattappana’s Position as the Commercial Capital of the High Ranges
content: Kattappana functions as the primary commercial and financial nerve center for the High Ranges of Idukki. Positioned adjacent to the world’s largest cardamom producing belts in Vandanmedu and Nedumkandam, the municipality handles thousands of tonnes of green cardamom, black pepper, cloves, and nutmeg through commercial grading facilities, curing smokehouses, and trading godowns.

Historically, Kattappana traders focused on bulk commodity auctions. Today, an ambitious new generation is launching branded consumer spice pouches, gourmet gift jars, and certified organic export packs. However, operating under the mistaken belief that an FSSAI license confers brand ownership exposes local businesses to trademark squatting by competitors in Kochi or Tamil Nadu.

callout.title: FSSAI License Does Not Grant Brand Monopoly
callout.text: FSSAI is a food hygiene license under the Food Safety and Standards Act. It does not stop competitors from copying your product name or packaging pouch. Only a registered trademark under the Trade Marks Act, 1999 guarantees brand ownership.

h2Sections.h2: Determining Your FoSCoS License Tier in Kattappana
content: Under FSSAI regulations, spice processing and packaging units must apply for the appropriate license tier based on capacity and annual turnover:

rows: Turnover under ₹12 Lakhs / up to 100 kg/day
Turnover ₹12 Lakhs to ₹20 Crores / up to 2 MT/day

h2Sections.h2: Nice Class Classification for Kattappana Spice Brands
content: Ensure your trademark application spans the appropriate international Nice classes to protect both goods and services:
checklist: Class 30 (Whole & Ground Spices): Green cardamom pods, black peppercorns, white pepper, ground spice powders (turmeric, chili, coriander), masala blends, seasonings, cloves, and cinnamon.
Class 29 (Preserved Produce & Pastes): Ginger-garlic pastes, spice marinades in oil, processed spice extracts, and dried culinary herbs.
Class 31 (Raw Agricultural Produce): Raw unprocessed agricultural seeds, raw spice berries prior to curing, and live cardamom saplings.
Class 35 (Wholesale Trade & E-Commerce): Operating a spice export trading house, wholesale auction agency, and online direct-to-consumer spice portal.

content: To launch your Kattappana packaged spice brand compliantly without product seizures or legal disputes:

Clear your brand name on IP India, file Form TM-A with Chennai Registry using an Udyam certificate (₹4,500 government fee), submit your FoSCoS application with water potability laboratory test reports, and print retail packaging strictly complying with FSSAI (Labelling and Display) Regulations.
checklist: 1. IP India Clearance: Confirm zero phonetic conflicts in Classes 30 and 35.
2. FoSCoS Laboratory Testing: Secure water test report and food product analysis from an NABL-accredited laboratory.
3. Mandatory Label Integration: Display 14-digit FSSAI number, vegetarian green symbol, net weight, batch number, and ™ mark.
4. MSME Cost Subsidy: Use Udyam certificate to save 50% on government trademark filing fees.

faqs.question: Can I print packaging pouches in Kattappana before my trademark is fully approved?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can use the ™ symbol on your retail packaging as soon as Form TM-A is submitted and an official Application Number is issued by the Trade Marks Registry. However, you cannot use the registered ® symbol until the final Registration Certificate is issued.

faqs.question: Is a laboratory water test report mandatory for an FSSAI State License in Kattappana?
faqs.answer: Yes. Any commercial spice processing or packaging facility applying for an FSSAI State License must submit a water test report from an NABL-accredited laboratory confirming potability according to IS 10500 standards.
